title: Mitigate tenant peering flaps causing cross-tenant DNS leakage in Dedicated clusters
creator: Marcus Li
description: Summary: Multiple Dedicated customers reported intermittent cross-tenant DNS resolution and connectivity errors after autoscaling and peering churn events. Impact: customer applications briefly resolved internal hostnames from other tenants' private zones, leading to failed service bindings and PII-risky telemetry. Scope: observed in Dedicated clusters using VPC peering + shared route exchange with Private DNS forwarding; affected ~3 customers during the incident window.
root_cause: Race condition in the peering controller when reconciling route and DNS namespace objects during rapid peering updates. The controller could apply route updates out-of-order relative to private DNS zone attachment, leaving transient forwarding entries that allowed other tenant DNS zones to be served until kube-dns reconciled. Additional contributor: concurrent netfilter/iptables rules updated by the node agent without a lock, which allowed short-lived rule combos that bypassed the intended namespacing enforcement.
repro_steps: 1) Create two Dedicated tenants with VPC peering and private hosted zones. 2) Trigger a peering reconfiguration (scale up or peering rebind). 3) Immediately run repeated DNS queries for tenant-local hostnames from nodes in the other tenant. 4) Observe TTLs and responses that match the other tenant's private zone for 10-30s before reconciliation.
workarounds: 1) If experiencing the issue: immediately toggle peering to force a full reconcile: `rctl peering restart <peering-id>` (internal tool). 2) Restart core-dns pods on affected clusters to clear cached/incorrect responses. 3) Temporarily disable automated route exchange until the safe update is applied. These mitigations reduce exposure while fix is deployed.
proposed_fix: 1) Make peering controller updates atomic: apply DNS zone attachment changes before route advertisements with a coordinator lock. 2) Add an iptables/netfilter update lock in the node agent to serialize rule changes and prevent transient permissive states. 3) Add a preflight validation step in the peering reconciler to reject partial updates when zone attachments are not confirmed. 4) Backfill e2e tests that simulate rapid peering churn and assert tenant DNS isolation. 5) Ship as patch release dedicated-2.3.1 with a config flag to opt into the safer update path.
tests: Unit tests for reconciler ordering, integration tests that spin up two tenant namespaces with fake DNS servers, and an e2e scenario in the staging fleet that performs 100 peering rebinds while asserting no cross-tenant DNS resolution. Added alerting for >1% cross-tenant NXDOMAIN anomalies to catch regressions.
rollback_plan: If rollout causes regressions, revert the peering controller image and node-agent change via canary rollback: target canary group -> monitor DNS isolation metrics for 30m -> roll back globally if >0.5% cross-tenant responses observed. Rollback playbook linked in attachments.
